gb2312.desc_en: Every hanzi in the 1980 national standard basic set — 6,763 characters across Levels 1 and 2.

gb2312-l1.desc_en: 3,755 frequently used characters, ordered by pinyin.

gb2312-l2.desc_en: 3,008 less frequently used characters, ordered by radical.

gbk-hanzi.desc_en: Every hanzi encoded by GBK, compatibility ideographs included.

gb12345.desc_en: Issued in 1990; the traditional-form counterpart to GB/T 2312.

gb18030-2022-l1.desc_en: The minimum mandatory conformance level for all products: every hanzi and radical in the BMP (27,584 characters).

gb18030-2022-l2.desc_en: Mandatory for system software: Level 1 plus the 196 General Standard characters that sit in the supplementary planes.

gb18030-2022-l3.desc_en: Required of government and public-service products: CJK Extensions A–F and the Kangxi radicals in full (88,115 characters).

tongyong-guifan.desc_en: The standard now in force, issued by the State Council in 2013: 8,105 characters in three levels.
tongyong-guifan.name_en: Table of General Standard Chinese Characters

tongyong-guifan-l1.desc_en: 3,500 characters — the working set for compulsory education and publishing.

tongyong-guifan-l3.desc_en: 1,605 characters used in surnames and given names, place names, and technical terminology.

changyong-3500.desc_en: Issued in 1988: 2,500 frequently used characters plus 1,000 less frequently used ones.
changyong-3500.name_en: List of Frequently Used Characters in Modern Chinese

changyong-2500.name_en: Frequently Used Characters in Modern Chinese (2500)

cichangyong-1000.name_en: Less Frequently Used Characters in Modern Chinese (1000)

tongyong-7000.name_en: List of Commonly Used Characters in Modern Chinese

yijiao-3500.desc_en: Appendix to the 2022 curriculum standard; 3,500 characters.

guji-yinshua.desc_en: The 2021 standard for characters used in printing ancient Chinese books.
guji-yinshua.name_en: Standard Glyph Forms for Ancient Book Printing

radicals-supplement.desc_en: The 115 assigned radical variants in U+2E80–2EF3.

hanyi-jianfan.desc_en: The simplified-plus-traditional coverage the Hanyi foundry quotes for its fonts.

fangzheng-jianfan.desc_en: The simplified-plus-traditional coverage the FounderType foundry quotes for its fonts.

tw-changyong-4808.name_en: Standard Forms of Common National Characters

tw-cichangyong-6343.name_en: Standard Forms of Less-Common National Characters

big5-changyong.desc_en: The Big5 frequently used range A440–C67E; 5,401 characters.

big5-cichangyong.desc_en: The Big5 less frequently used range C940–F9D5.

big5.desc_en: Both ranges combined, de-duplicated by Unicode code point.

bopomofo.desc_en: Bopomofo and its extensions, as used for Min Nan and Hakka.

hk-changyong.desc_en: The Hong Kong Education Bureau's table of standard character forms.
hk-changyong.name_en: List of Graphemes of Commonly-Used Chinese Characters

hkscs.name_en: Hong Kong Supplementary Character Set Hanzi

hk-suppchara.desc_en: The Education Bureau's commonly used supplementary characters, Levels 1–6.
hk-suppchara.name_en: Hong Kong Supplementary Characters in Common Use

jisx0208-nonkanji.desc_en: Kana, symbols, and Roman, Greek and Cyrillic letters.

jisx0208-l1.desc_en: 2,965 Level 1 kanji, ordered by on'yomi reading.

jisx0213-l3.desc_en: The kanji added on plane 1 by the 2000/2004 extensions.

joyo.desc_en: The 2,136 kanji in general use today, per the 2010 Cabinet notification.

kyoiku.desc_en: The 1,026 elementary-school kanji in the by-grade allocation table in force since 2020.

jinmeiyo.desc_en: Kanji outside the Joyo set permitted in personal names, per the appendix to the Family Register Act rules (2026 additions included).

jisx0201.desc_en: Roman characters and halfwidth kana — the 7-bit / 8-bit single-byte set.

ksx1001-hangul.desc_en: The 2,350 syllables in common use in modern Korean.

ksx1001-hanja.desc_en: 4,888 hanja, with duplicated hanja mapped into the compatibility block.

ksx1001-symbols.desc_en: The non-hangul, non-hanja part: symbols, letters, Japanese kana and the like.

hangul-jamo.desc_en: Conjoining hangul jamo, U+1100–11FF, archaic letters included.

iicore.desc_en: An ISO/IEC 10646 annex: a core han set aimed at resource-constrained environments.

unihan-core-2020.desc_en: The Unihan database's core set for modern general use, covering Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Vietnamese usage as well as Hong Kong and Taiwan.

wgl4.desc_en: Microsoft's pan-European character set: 650 code points (the commonly cited 652 counts two duplicated glyphs).

latin-ext-a.desc_en: U+0100–017F, the Central and Eastern European characters.

cyrillic.desc_en: The characters actually needed to write Russian, Ukrainian, Belarusian, Serbian, Macedonian and Bulgarian. Old Church Slavonic letters and minority-language extensions are excluded — coverage of the whole U+0400–04FF block is reported separately in a font's Unicode blocks section.

viet-latin.desc_en: Every letter of Vietnamese quốc ngữ: basic Latin, the accented letters from Latin-1 and Latin Extended-A/B, and Latin Extended Additional U+1EA0–1EF9.

cp437.desc_en: The DOS and retro-terminal character set, graphics interpretation: 255 characters, 0x01–0xFF.

box-drawing.desc_en: U+2500–257F, the terminal rules and table borders.

block-elements.desc_en: U+2580–259F, the solid and shaded terminal blocks.

powerline.desc_en: The 41 symbols Powerline and its extensions occupy in the private use area, U+E0A0–E0D4.

greek.desc_en: The characters actually needed to write modern Greek: the alphabet, final sigma, accented vowels and diaeresis forms, and the tonos marks. Coptic and archaic letters are excluded — coverage of the whole U+0370–03FF block is reported separately in a font's Unicode blocks section.

arabic.desc_en: The 92 characters actually needed to write Arabic, Persian and Urdu: the basic letters and tatweel, everyday vowel marks, both digit sets, common punctuation, and the letters specific to Persian and Urdu. Quranic annotation marks and rare regional letters are excluded — coverage of the whole U+0600–06FF block is reported separately in a font's Unicode blocks section.
